title: What’s your favorite leveling up system?
author: Asleep-Stop-9919
selftext:
Hi,

So i really love the leveling up system of skyrim.  
Hit with a one handed sword and u gain exp in that. Block with a shield and u get exp in that and so on…

I also love the leveling system of souls games.  
Preferably i would like to sell some stuff i don’t need to have more currency to level up more.

I guess my favorite way would be one, where i could raid. Take everything with me and then sell like 90% of it to get currency to level up. But i also wouldn’t wanna give up the leveling system of skyrim.

I feel like for gamers it’s instantly rewarding when you know that your fighting itself is making you stronger.   
In God of War (classics) for instance u would get those red orbs each time u’d kill an enemy.  
So therefore i loved running around and killing side enemies as well because i wanted to become as op as possible.

I was wondering today what my perfect leveling up system in an RPG would look like. I don’t want to exchange one for the other but at the same time i don’t want to loose the profits of one or the other.

Thanks for reading if u came this far.  
What do u think? Are my eyes bigger than my stomach, is there beauty in leaving something valueable?  
And what is your favorite way of leveling up? What would u recommend? 😇

comments.author: alanbdee
comments.body: I think Skyrim is my favorite type. Maybe with a bit of Subnautica where you have limited space to carry things and things are different sizes. I've sort of always hated the idea of showing up at a shop with 30 sets of armor to sell. Like, dude ain't carrying that many chest plates.

replies.author: Asleep-Stop-9919
replies.body:
Really? Haha  
For me it was always the opposite, i mean what u r saying is totally logical but all i wanted to do was to go into a cave, kill everybody, mine ore, fast travel and then sell everything. I felt like even if i only get like 3 coins for a sword it wouldn’t matter bcs i am looting every inch of that place anyway. Again ur point makes way more sense. But i’ll still die with mine 😂 it was just so much fun

comments.author: DeanRayGames
comments.body: My favorite leveling up system I've ever experienced in any RPG was Chrono Cross!

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body:
I don't generally like kill-based XP systems because they funnel all the game's possibilities into one objective. Turns the game into a grind.

Mission based XP systems do the same thing; the game becomes all about completing quests and everything outside of that is either for money or just flavor.

Skyrim is great because it's per skill and based on the action itself not the outcome. It's very similar to Runescape. That animates the world somewhat.

Generally speaking, though, I prefer D&D-style milestone leveling, because it takes the XP slot machine out of the game altogether. But you need a DM for that.

I love RPGs but these days I'm wondering if I'm over the whole XP, leveling, hit points, that kind of thing altogether. It seems pretty overdone to me, and I think with the tech we have now, we can make no-stat-sheet games where you get a sense of progression from the world being cumulatively responsive to your achievements... And where things like health and energy are part of how your character's body is simulated, not just a percentage bar.

comments.author: Arcodiant
comments.body: My favourite mechanism was very niche, but it was in Tron 2.0. Each skill/upgrade/ability was a program you loaded into a limited memory space, and came in alpha/beta/gold versions. The exact memory you had available varied between game levels, but it was always a ring of blocks with gaps in it. Alpha versions of skills took 3 blocks, while gold only took one, so in addition to being better, gold skills took less space so you could have more (and they'd fit into the weird gaps in memory). Upgrades were limited pickups, so you'd get X skill upgrades for each map you finished.
